history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration review its existing processes under the current legal framework in cases where the Organization has suffered a financial loss due to possible gross negligence, to enforce accountability, where appropriate.
history.administration_response: The Administration considers this recommendation to be implemented. The Administration conducted a review of existing processes in cases in which the Organization has suffered a financial loss. These processes clarify that the occurrence of a financial loss does not automatically imply gross negligence. Investigations by OIOS are initiated only when there is evidence suggesting gross negligence. OIOS receives investigation requests from the Administration, referrals from internal audits and confidential reports of waste, fraud or mismanagement through the OIOS hotline. When assessing a report, indications of either significant financial loss or reputational risk to the Organization are considered as part of the OIOS investigation intake criteria and result in priority investigation. Where an investigation supports the complaint, an investigation report is sent to the Office of Human Resources for review and consideration of disciplinary action. Staff rule 10.1 (b) provides for the imposition of the administrative measure of financial recovery in cases of established misconduct that is determined to be wilful, reckless or grossly negligent. All quantifiable loss to the Organization is specified for recovery in appropriate cases. The Office of Human Resources prioritizes cases that entail significant financial loss or reputational risk to the Organization. When a disciplinary process is initiated, each relevant entity is notified of the pending process and requested to provide an update on the status of the staff member’s employment. This facilitates the timely withholding of final entitlements, as appropriate, in cases in which the staff member resigns in the middle of the disciplinary process. In some cases, the transmission of the necessary documentation to the United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund may be withheld to delay the payment of a withdrawal settlement or pension entitlements. In addition, OIOS is reviewing the case referred to by the Board of Auditors, as requested in General Assembly resolution 79/246.
history.board_assessment: Given that there remains a lack of clear guidelines for the investigation of financial losses incurred by the United Nations, the Board considers the recommendation to be under implementation.
